//deploy:passport:manual: BREAK GLASS ONLY — `deploy:passport:manual` is not how the Passport demo
ships any more. https://midnightpassport.com is deployed by
.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml, from a published GitHub release, and
only from a commit that is an ancestor of origin/main. The rule the project
lead asked for is that what is on main is what is deployed, and a laptop
running `vercel deploy` is exactly what breaks it.
It was renamed from `deploy:passport` rather than deleted, because GitHub
Actions can itself be unavailable. What it does NOT do is the point: no
typecheck, no unit tests, no PWA check, no end-to-end run, and no check
that what it uploads corresponds to any commit — it ships whatever is on
disk, uncommitted changes included.
Its VITE_* values are duplicated in deploy-demo.yml's `env:` block, which
is the copy that ships. Change both together.
VITE_MIDNIGHT_PROVING_URL and VITE_SPONSOR_URL take a comma-separated,
ORDERED list since 2026/08/31, tried left to right per request. The 1AM
stagenet gateway is second and deliberately so; deploy-demo.yml carries the
measurement that decided the order. VITE_FUNDER_URL stays a single URL:
/register-alias and /fund-account exist nowhere but our balancer.
docs/demo/deployment.md is the whole procedure: cutting a release, the
three repository secrets, and rolling back with `vercel promote`.
The other deploy:* scripts are unchanged — only the Passport demo has
continuous deployment so far.

//dependencies: NOTHING AT THE ROOT IMPORTS ANY OF THESE. Every name below is resolution
control: it decides which copy npm hoists, so that each workspace gets the
one it needs. The versions are exact rather than ranged because a caret
resolves against whatever else is present, and this tree is large enough
that it drifts: `^8.0.3` once resolved to ledger-v8 8.1.1 here while a
nested consumer held 8.1.0, and two ledger-v8 copies make `tsc` emit pages
of 'ZswapSecretKeys is not assignable to ZswapSecretKeys'.
TWO MIDNIGHT STACKS LIVE IN ONE INSTALL, and that is what the block below
is for. `examples/passport-demo` is on LEDGER-9 — ledger-v9 1.0.0-rc.3,
midnight-js 5.0.0-beta.7, compact-runtime 0.19.0-rc.0, compact-js
2.5.5-rc.8, wallet-sdk 2.0.0-beta.2 — because that is what stagenet runs.
`examples/passport-funder` is on LEDGER-8: midnight-js 4.0.4,
compact-runtime 0.16.0, ledger-v8 8.0.3, and the ledger-8 wallet SDK.
npm hoists one copy of each name to the root and nests the rest, and it
hoists on FIRST CLAIM, not on merit. So the ledger-9 names are declared
here, which makes the DEMO's copies the hoisted ones; the funder's ledger-8
copies nest underneath the funder, where only it can reach them. The
ledger-8 wallet-sdk, ledger-v8 8.1.0, zswap, and wallet-api pins are the
other half of the same arrangement.
The check is one command:
npm ls @midnight-ntwrk/compact-runtime
It must report exactly ONE copy at the root, 0.19.0-rc.0, with
`passport-demo` deduped onto it, and the funder's 0.16.0 nested under
`passport-funder`. Measured on 2026/09/15, that is what it reports.
Why duplicates are fatal rather than untidy. A generated Compact contract
module opens with `import * as __compactRuntime from '@midnight-ntwrk/
compact-runtime'` and then `__compactRuntime.checkRuntimeVersion('<exact
version>')`. Node and the bundler both resolve that specifier from the
MODULE's directory, walking upwards — so which copy a contract gets is
decided by where the contract file sits, not by which workspace asked for
it. And midnight-js decodes contract state through `ChargedState`: two
copies of the runtime are two `ChargedState` classes, and an `instanceof`
check then fails on objects that are correct in every other respect. Two
copies of compact-js are two `CompactContext` TypeId symbols, and
`deployContract` dies with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading
'ctor')` — measured against stagenet on 2026/08/24.
So if you change anything here, re-run the demo's own gates: its typecheck,
its `test:coverage`, and a `vite build`.
//overrides: Added by the Passport migration. Three entries; each says what it changes
and why it is safe.
`vite` `^6.0.0`. The root's `vitest` reaches Vite through `vite-node`, whose
range is `^5 || ^6 || ^7`, so npm hoists Vite 7 to the root and nests 6.x
under each workspace that asks for `^6`. That is two Vite instances in one
build: `@vitejs/plugin-react` binds to the hoisted 7 while the app runs 6,
and `examples/passport-demo`'s service-worker stamping plugin then dies with
`ENOENT … dist/sw.js` at `closeBundle`. Every workspace here already asks
for `^6`; this only stops `vite-node` from dragging a second major in.
`@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk-utilities` 1.2.1. Nothing declares this
directly — it arrives transitively. wallet-sdk 2.0.0-beta.2 pins 1.2.0, a
publish that does not export `Clock`; wallet-sdk-facade imports `Clock`, so
the wallet dies at build time with the rollup error 'Clock is not exported
by …/wallet-sdk-utilities/dist/index.js'. 1.2.1 is the fixed publish and is
otherwise identical. It is written globally because both surgical forms were
tried and neither reaches the copy inside
node_modules/@midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk/node_modules, which is where the
beta tree lives and where the broken copy is.
`@scure/base` 2.3.0, SCOPED to the two address-format packages. A freshly
resolved tree gives them 2.4.0, which reimposes bech32's classic
90-character limit on bech32m. Midnight shielded addresses are 133
characters, so `MidnightBech32m.parse` throws 'invalid string length 133,
expected (8..90)' and the app reports a valid stagenet shielded address as
'not a Midnight address'. Caught by e2e/send-assets.spec.ts and reproduced
outside the browser before pinning; 2.3.0 is what the live site was built
against.
The scoping is the point. Written globally, it also moves @polkadot's copy
off 1.2.6, and `@polkadot/util-crypto` imports a `utils` export that 2.x
does not have — the build then fails with '"utils" is not exported by
@scure/base'. So the two packages that need 2.3.0 get it and nothing else
does.
